Author: @Ipo_Ooped_Maself
Content: I have a real problem with this business model.If aldi is able to not only dictate manufacturer and farmer pricing, as well as speed and schedule of delivery and production.But then, they're also able to increase profits and pricing.Whenever they choose, without those benefits flowing down the pipeline to the producers and manufacturers of the goods.That's a big issue that's not right. Now I'm no socialist, and certainly not a Communist, absolutely not. Those things are evil. However, in the free market, one person in a 2 party or multi-party deal should not be able to dictate the arrangement for everyone. That is not free trade. That is a controlled hostile market. I don't see the point of participating in that. To be honest, it doesn't matter how large the market share is Aldi. Is still Aldi, it's not Kroger or Myers or Walmart. I know many people who don't shop at Aldi. Just because of the reputation, it's considered a poverty store. I used to shop at Aldi. When prices were actually low 10 or 15 years ago, you could go in there and get goods for drastically lower prices than you could anywhere else. And it was worth it now. You might save 10 or 15 cents on an item. Maybe 25 or 50 cents here or there. But the savings don't add up enough to justify leaving your normal market. And since they don't sell brand name goods most of the time, I'm not willing to break brand loyalty for a savings, that's less than 30%. If I have a $300 car to groceries, I want that to be a 2. Two hundred dollar cart at aldi's, or I don't see the point in going and getting non brand name goods.I trust those brand names to give me food.That is safe for me.And my family and tastes up to my expectations.I also don't like the idea of buying goods from a store that treats its farmers in a hostile manner.And holds them to unreasonable expectations with no reward.I guess i'm done doing business with aldi

There’s an old saying: two people can keep a secret as long as one of them is dead. These “kidnappers” were amateurs. They were smart in some ways and dumb in others. 

The main thing is that kidnapping an important person isn’t enough. You have to put just as much (if not more) energy and terror into the immediate family so that they don’t contact the police. This is something most kidnappers really suck at and always what ends up getting them caught. 

Also, don’t have living co-conspirators. The living part being the imperative word. 

That said, kidnapping is a really dumb way to make money. In order to really succeed at it, you have to be incredibly sharp. There are much safer and easier ways of (legally!) making large sums of money, at least for people living in civilized / rule of law countries if you’re smart. Why bother risking prison?

Author: @ImKinoNichtSabbeln
Content:
Around 27:27, the banknote is wrong.

Depicted is a 500 DM note from the fourth DM series "BBK III" (motives: Significant Germans) issued from 1st Octobre1990 onwards.

1971, BBk III did neither exit, nor was even imagined.
Instead, in 1971 the series BBk I (excerpts from important German paintings - by chance: people) was valid (1961-1990).

FYI, the 2 series before BBk I, series "Bank deutscher Länder", and the in the USA printed initial series were completely different, too.
Not only in the motives, and colours, but even the measurements were different between the series.

Showing a BBk III banknote instead of a BBk I one, is like saying "they used this Chrysler Sedan" while showing a Mercedes SUV: it's blatantly wrong.

PS:
There was even strictly secret, never released reserve series BBk II printed in just slightly reduced volume to enable an immediate substitution of BBk I, if necessary.
Details incl. the motives were released just after 2010.

Background: Back then, West Germany feared, that East Germany would  somevdsy (war) zake thevchsnce to devalue the successful DM by spreading counterfeit BBk I banknotes in huge volume.
In that case, the West-German government coukd have announced the invalidaty of BBk I for commercial use, and immediately distributed BBk II, instead.
Banknotes of BBk II were stored, maintained and checked, and even continuously printed upto 1988.

The BBk II banknotes were kept _very_ secret and _very_ safe.

Content:
So the dude making "less than 2000 DM" per month(04:40) in 1971, right? Just to give an idea of how much that is in USD of today - $4573,21. Since there has been a bunch going on in the intervening years in European currency that I wanted to avoid having to directly factor in, I hitched a ride on the USD from then using inflation, $1 in 1971 was todays equivalent of $7,94 - DM2000 in 1971 was $574,7 which brings us to $4573.21 today. 
$4573 is €3900 which is a fairly nice chunk of cash, it's more than the current average income in NL of €3666(right now) which makes the dude a greedy bastard. "less than" in the text could theoretically mean $1/yr but despite the deficient wording and lack of actual numbers here I'm going to assume "less than" really means "close to" - since otherwise whoever wrote this bit really should pack up and do something else. I couldn't find any info on the actual salary of Paul Kron to verify the amount so I have no idea where the info was pulled from for this video - but the numbers are fairly realistic so I'm assuming they are from some reasonably good source, it passes the "smell test".
